note.note:
History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male lawyer with history of hypothyroidism (stopped levothyroxine) presents with 3–4 months of low mood, fatigue, anorexia and 1-stone unintentional weight loss (over ~6 months), plus situational palpitations/subjective breathlessness in elevators; normal bowels; clinician arranged baseline blood tests and safety-net advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Reduced appetite and energy.  
• Onset/progression:  
  – Appetite loss and low energy began ≈3.5 months ago (coincided with job change).  
  – Weight loss (~1 stone/6 kg) has occurred gradually over ≈6 months.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Low mood; “feeling down,” nothing feels right.  
  – Decreased libido (“wife complaining about nightly activities”).  
  – Episodic palpitations and “can’t breathe” sensation, especially in lifts; no chest pain; no dyspnoea on walking a mile (though currently sedentary).  
  – Occasional nausea without vomiting.  
  – Headaches at work.  
• Gastrointestinal review: Normal bowel motions; no diarrhoea, blood or mucus; no abdominal pain; no acid reflux.  
• Respiratory review: No chronic cough; exertional capacity preserved.  
• Cardiovascular review: Palpitations situational; denies chest pain.  
• Neurological review: No focal deficits reported.  
• Constitutional: Unintentional weight loss, fatigue.  
• Pertinent negatives: No vomiting, night sweats, fever, or overt exertional dyspnoea.

Past Medical History:
• Primary hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).  
  – Previously treated with levothyroxine; patient stopped “since I changed doctor.”  
  – No recent thyroid function blood tests.  
• No other chronic illnesses mentioned.

Medications:
• Levothyroxine – stopped; last use “months ago” (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
• Not discussed. (Missing)

Social History:
• Occupation: Lawyer; moved to a new law firm ~3.5 months ago (possible stressor).  
• Marital status: Married.  
• Exercise: Currently minimal; reports not walking much lately.  
• Tobacco, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed. (Missing)  
• Financial/lifestyle factors: None mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• No physical examination performed during video visit.  
• No vitals available.

Investigations:
• None to date.  
• Plan: “General set of bloods” ordered – CBC, renal profile, liver profile, thyroid function tests, vitamin levels (per transcript).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Unintentional weight loss, anorexia, fatigue, low mood  
  – Possible major depressive disorder, relapse of hypothyroidism, anaemia or other systemic disease.  
  – Plan:  
    • Arrange baseline blood tests (CBC, renal, liver, thyroid profile, vitamins).  
    • Consider further evaluation (e.g., physical examination, additional labs or imaging) once results available.  
    • Safety-net: If new chest pain, persistent vomiting, or change in bowel habit, attend A&E or re-contact service.  

Issue 2: Episodic palpitations/breathlessness in lifts  
  – Likely situational anxiety/panic vs. arrhythmia.  
  – Plan:  
    • Monitor frequency/severity.  
    • If palpitations become persistent, severe, or are associated with chest pain/syncope, seek urgent care.  
    • Reassess after baseline investigations.

Issue 3: History of untreated hypothyroidism  
  – Stopped levothyroxine; current thyroid status unknown.  
  – Plan:  
    • Check thyroid function tests with current blood panel.  
    • If hypothyroid, restart levothyroxine per guidelines and arrange endocrinology or primary-care follow-up.

General advice:  
• Contact support line (number in app) to schedule blood draw; results to be sent via text prompting follow-up appointment.  
• Encourage gradual return to light activity as tolerated.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Major depressive disorder – High likelihood: Persistent low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight change, fatigue, situational anxiety symptoms; temporal link to job change.  
2. Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism – Moderate likelihood: History of underactive thyroid and cessation of replacement therapy; compatible with fatigue and low mood, though weight loss is atypical.  
3. Iron-deficiency or other anaemia – Moderate likelihood: Fatigue, headaches, possible reduced exercise tolerance; will be assessed with CBC.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected elements: Allergies, current medication list with doses, comprehensive substance use history, vitals, physical examination.  
• Transcript/DDx conflicts: Weight loss favors hyperthyroidism or depression more than hypothyroidism (noted in DDx).  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional overlaps/inaudible phrases but core information understandable.
